reason:
Under the feasibility lens the idea as specified cannot be tested faithfully, and it conflicts with four shipped stages.

(1) THE LAB CANNOT REPLAY THE INSERTION POINT. The change inserts nodes post-ILP and before the motion relink, so that relink, gap, gap2, ef and stitch see them. The replay lab starts at the ckpt, which is already post-relink, post-gap and post-gap2. Its docstring (experiments/l2_daughternet/replay/replay.py, lines 1-12) says raw->ckpt is NOT replayed, because DeepCenter scores exist only at raw nodes. The gap-close veto and gap2 therefore cannot be rerun with new nodes. anatomy.relink_rerun reruns the relink alone, so a 'raw + new nodes -> relink -> tail' run would skip gap close and gap2 for EVERY node, not just the new ones. It would no longer reproduce the exp39 control (0.9143), and the delta would be confounded. Every shipped lab patch (leafprune, ef, stitch, swapfix, divinsert) acts post-ckpt or post-tail for exactly this reason.

(2) THE PEAK POOL IS MISSING, AND THE LAB POOL WOULD NOT MATCH THE KERNEL'S. The 0.90 cache exists only on friend A's machine: 1,015,461 peaks, +23.9% of nodes, up to 73% in one video. It is not on the laptop and not a Kaggle dataset. Its identity is primary_only=True (tools/recover_daughters.py lines 145-156). The kernel detector is the 2-seed ensemble, and the only in-kernel sub-threshold source is x138's lowdet dump (>=0.3, int16, unrefined). A 0.90 cut on one model's heatmap is not the same set as a 0.90 cut on the fused map. Rebuilding a kernel-identical pool on 199 train videos would take about 7 min per movie (exp51 took 1,713 s for 4 movies), about 16-20 of the ~20 Kaggle GPU hours left, so only friend A's GPU can do it.

(3) CONFLICTS WITH SHIPPED STAGES. All four are mechanical and would erase or distort the insertions.
- Leaf prune 0.3 (build_probe_kernel.py lines 357-402) removes any leaf whose single in-edge has a finite prob < 0.3. The relink stores 0.0 for pairs the network never scored, so every tracklet end on an inserted node loses its last node.
- The edge filter targets exactly finite prob < 0.3 relink edges when the ILP linked the node elsewhere (alt modes). An existing track end u that the ILP had continued elsewhere gets u->q dropped and relinked to its ILP successor, which undoes the fill.
- Safe divisions (divnet_rerank: orphan starts within 12 um, sister >= 5 um) and divinsert steal treat any unattached inserted start 4.5-12 um from a track as a daughter candidate. That is new division-FP exposure, and division FP is already 43 vs 23 TP.
- min_track_len 6 kills inserted runs that stay unattached. The research found the reachable (>7 um) holes are persistent side_far runs, so attachment is exactly what fails.

(4) THE COORDINATE FRAMES WOULD MIX WITH THE HEAD. With the coordhead port, kept nodes are float-refined (mean shift 0.74 um, max 1.6 um), while lowdet peaks are unrefined int16. That shift is comparable to the refined rule's |q - midpoint| < 2 um, and it biases the clearance rule. The lowdet patch also anchors on the same coord_offset line as the head patch (x122 failed silently from patch order).

The research lens already refuted the mechanism: 4-6 um holes are same-blob offsets, and the sandwich passes 40% of random points. Porting the refined variant (valley + chain) is feasible, but it needs about 1 day of lab code, about 0.5-1 day of kernel port, and a friend-A upload before step 0. That leaves no slack before a 27-28 Sep probe, and it competes with the coordhead port and B35 for the same days.
fix_if_any:
Make it a post-ckpt stage the lab can replay, and cut the stage conflicts.
(a) Position: after the ckpt, before safe divisions. The ckpt nodes plus new peaks go through motion_relink_edges (the learned map from raw), and the tail runs as usual. Alternatively attach chains only as end->start bridges, like stitch or gapfill.
(b) Edges: every edge touching an inserted node carries edge_prob None plus a 'holefill' flag. None exempts it from leaf prune and ef by construction.
(c) Divisions: inserted nodes are ineligible as safe-division or divinsert daughters (div_insert already takes gap_synthetic flags; add one).
(d) Chains: only chains of 3 or more that attach at both ends, or that reach 6 or more nodes, so min_track_len cannot silently delete them.
(e) Pool parity: primary-only 0.90 peaks in both lab and kernel. Add a primary-only lowdet dump patch placed BEFORE the coordhead patch, and compare in refined coordinates (apply the head to the peaks, or compare against pre-refinement node positions).
(f) Friend A uploads peaks90/*.npz as a private Kaggle dataset (small: int16 tzyx + prob). Step 0 and the valley test run on a Kaggle CPU kernel with the competition zarr, about 1 h for about 20k frames with the gaussian.
Go only if the step-0 counts from the research refinement pass: coverage >= 20% of >7 um holes in both embryos, false-flank rate <= 10%, <= +1% nodes. Otherwise drop it and spend the days on coordhead + same-blob duplicate merging.
realistic_public_gain: Original rule: <= 0 (duplicates on same-blob holes plus a certain node penalty, and leaf prune / ef would strip most fills anyway). Repaired distinct-nucleus, post-ckpt variant: 0 to +0.002 public (local +0.001 to +0.004 before a >= 50% haircut), with a real risk that it cannot be confirmed and probed before 29 Sep.
